account: Taichung's Environmental Protection Bureau (EPB) installed its AI smoke-recognition system, air micro-sensors and cameras beside Hugan Road, Dadu District. That followed a March 2025 complaint about smoke from a dumping spot. CNA reports that shortly after 08:00 on 4 July 2025 the instruments flagged abnormal air quality. Inspectors found dumped waste burning. The system recorded the same man in July and August. His motorcycle plate was too faded to read. So inspectors collected neighbors' closed-circuit television (CCTV) and dashcam footage. A Wuri Precinct officer recognized a 74-year-old man surnamed Zhao, who confessed. On 13 September 2025 the EPB announced a fine of up to NT$100,000 under the Air Pollution Control Act. It asked the land manager to clear the site.

ai_role.statement: The AI smoke-recognition system and micro-sensors supplied the detection that sent inspectors to the burning site. CNA dates it first to 4 July 2025, then repeatedly in July and August. It also supplied the video that recorded the offender. It could not read his faded motorcycle plate. So identification came from private CCTV, dashcam footage and a police officer's recognition of a local resident. The system's contribution is detection and documentation. Removal of the source depended on human investigation. No measured air-quality change or proven counterfactual is reported. So the record sits at protective response with prevention unproven rather than specific harm prevented.
